reviews.body:
Thanks for fixing the normal `stop + tool_calls` path. I found and reproduced an edge-case regression on head `244b835`.

`anthropic_stop_reason()` checks the **mapped** reason for `end_turn`, but `_STOP_REASON_MAP` maps both `content_filter` and `unknown` to `end_turn` as well as normal `stop`. As a result, a content-filtered response carrying tool calls is changed to `tool_use`.

Minimal reproduction using `ModelOutput.for_tool_call('gemini', 'read_file', {'path': 'a.py'})` with `output.choices[0].stop_reason = 'content_filter'`:

```text
expected Anthropic stop_reason: end_turn
actual Anthropic stop_reason: tool_use
```

This can make an Anthropic client continue with tool execution after a content-filter termination. Please apply the compensation only when the original EvalScope stop reason is `stop`, preserving `content_filter`, `unknown`, and truncation semantics. Please also add non-streaming and SSE regression tests for `content_filter + tool_calls`.

comments.body:
Thanks for reproducing this, @Yunnglin. Fixed in the new commit: `anthropic_stop_reason()` now applies the `tool_use` compensation only when the original EvalScope stop reason is `stop`, so `content_filter`, `unknown` and truncation keep their mapped Anthropic value (`end_turn` / `max_tokens`). Added non-streaming and SSE regression tests for `content_filter + tool_calls` and `unknown + tool_calls`; they fail on the previous head and pass now.

This reply was drafted by an AI agent (Claude) working on behalf of the PR author.
